result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password**\. It's an excellent balance of security, ease of use, shared passwords and team administration.

However, **Bitwarden** is arguably the better choice if keeping costs down is your priority.

Here are my top picks.

## Best password managers for small teams

![Get to know 1Password for Mac | 1Password Support](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/C4U7UvvWr1lsit0fdwRMADZs7wYIji_AIA_d_hCeSHTTS1dPoJwwNeSzAPqWszRkpvDsM-p6I-6bznHJsD41eDQWYBj0MySy4qOfvgyzlD_4z3rPSGN9LVxo1hBQTb8qLml3yarSFkZEwcSqyJe7UAnBKtGHsXMSYuWNAwGS3UO1kE8Ogcbnaa14C9ioehoa?purpose=fullsize)

(Best overall)

**1\. 1Password**

Best for teams that want something polished and easy to manage.

- Shared vaults for departments and projects
- Granular access permissions
- Admin controls and activity reporting
- Excellent browser and mobile apps
- Easy onboarding and offboarding

Teams Starter Pack: US\$24.95/month for up to 10 people. Business: US\$8.99/user/month, annually.

[1Password business plans](https://1password.com/business)

---

![The best password managers in 2026 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/NzVuMgIchg5mHs-Kr9143cu9YVcLD78U-cfqnnpzpdksR6kB5LPVR6OyqUe0J0PAWilFgVX5RafeZ-AzNa_G6WUPgI8J1U4oAahEfqnQQL2SaxhVwFg9jy1o1kVewXMyq40iQ1cCkpkzpsh_DQntfgs6e3PLRpQFbO3dRcV-HQGbTSkVwYxuDvCJM657Aw6_?purpose=fullsize)

(Best value)

**2\. Bitwarden**

Best for smaller businesses wanting strong security without spending much.

- Shared organisational vaults
- User and group management
- Open-source software
- Security and event logs
- Self-hosting options

Teams: US\$4/user/month, billed annually.

[Bitwarden business plans](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

Best for businesses wanting additional security administration.

- Shared team folders
- Role-based access
- Detailed administrative controls
- Security monitoring
- Additional privileged access management options

Business Starter: approximately US\$2/user/month; check eligibility and limits.

[Keeper business plans](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![The best password managers in 2025 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/S30I88layvxbkaDwXaWP5XnJ7U511ARCXJEcDjYd8i8QoMbXMBiKKYXroCriJ7kBR0oi7lM-NLlyOXMHqaLP4YKGj6rWlLsTvfSS4pKj24h_up7wZjWKu6xYF8rT-_7bc8XbvU4PlaIDiwcj88cnT8GVhbZrDMRuBptQttvTl2oiFqpoAxV9-pe3un--FrSZ?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

Best for privacy-conscious teams.

- End-to-end encrypted vaults
- Secure sharing
- Email aliases
- Open-source applications
- Business administration features

Business pricing depends on the plan.

[Proton Pass business plans](https://proton.me/business/pass)

The pricing and feature comparisons are based on November 2026 listings. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.openideurope.eu](https://www.openideurope.eu/reviews/password-managers-for-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[cybercred.com.au](https://cybercred.com.au/articles/password-managers-compared-for-small-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My comparison

| Feature | 1Password | Bitwarden | Keeper |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Ease of use | Excellent | Very good | Very good |
| Shared passwords | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Team permissions | Excellent | Good | Excellent |
| Admin controls | Excellent | Good | Excellent |
| Budget friendly | Good | Excellent | Excellent |
| Self-hosting | No | Yes | No |


## What I'd prioritise

For a small business, make sure your chosen password manager supports\:

1. **Shared vaults\:** Everyone can access the credentials they need without sharing passwords through email or Slack.
2. **Individual accounts\:** Every employee has their own login.
3. **Access revocation\:** Remove someone's access immediately when they leave.
4. **Two-factor authentication\:** Protect the password manager itself.
5. **Audit logs\:** See who accessed or changed shared credentials.
6. **Role-based permissions\:** Not everyone should have access to every company password.

---

## A couple of questions to narrow it down

I'd like to recommend the right one rather than simply the most popular one.

**1\. How big is your team?**

**2\. What does your business primarily use?**

**3\. What's most important?**

---

**4\. Approximate monthly budget?**
